Department of Interior June 28, 1972
Page Six
NPS is also charged with the administration of "recreational areas" which, like the land areas referenced above, are designated by specific Congressional enactment, generally have somewhat unique natural characteristics and receive high density public use. Unlike the areas noted above, the primary purpose of recreational areas is that of public recreation.
Based on its experience in administering the above described areas and in light of the Congressional emphasis on the stewardship function and the high density use which is common in such areas, NPS has determined that ORRV use can best be regulated by confining such use to specifically designated areas. In light of the Park Service's substantial personnel resources, this regulatory approach has apparently been enforceable. This "prohibited except where specifically permitted" regulatory approach would apparently be carried forward by the regulations under the Executive Order. In light of the unique characteristics of the land areas involved, the Congressional emphasis on preservation, the high density use and the existence of adequate enforcement personnel, the Association agrees that, with respect to the lands described above, the aforementioned regulatory approach is appropriate.
